attribution_limitations: The abstract places one hospitalization for preterm labour in week 29, while the case text describes admissions at 28 weeks and "a week later". The source does not identify the week 29 hospitalization with either admission, so it is kept separate; this is not a source conflict because no single admission is given two different times.
Anchors of the relative times "3 days later" (after the 24-week admission), "a week later" and "6 months later" are not named literally.

The discussion says labour progression was delayed for 8 weeks; the case text gives admissions at 24, 28 and about 29 weeks and delivery at 32 weeks and 4 days, without naming the start of the 8 weeks.

Apgar scores are given for quadruplets A to D, but the Apgar time point is not stated, and apart from the pronoun "she" for quadruplet B the mapping of the one boy and three girls to individual quadruplets is not stated.
The abstract summarizes the neonates as weighing "between 1800 to 2100 gram" with "normal Apgar score", while the case text gives 1810 to 2100 gram and an Apgar score of 6-7 for quadruplet B.
Which hospitalization the two doses of betamethasone were given in is not named; the sentence follows the 28-week admission with "also".

"Her last pregnancy" in the pregnancy-test sentence is not named as the 3rd pregnancy; the e03 to e04 order rests on "last" referring to the latest of the three described prior pregnancies (ages 28, two years later, 32).
Discussion paragraphs mainly describe cited published cases; only sentences literally about "the reported patient" or "our patient" were used for the index patient.

claims.text: A 34-year-old woman, G4 L2 Ab1, who had married her cousin, had two prior normal vaginal deliveries and one first-trimester abortion. Using withdrawal contraception, she had no menstruation during breastfeeding and 6 months after her last pregnancy, and a pregnancy test was requested. The positive result led to an ultrasound study showing a 10-week spontaneous gestation with 4 gestational sacs and 4 fetuses, with no family history of multiple pregnancies.
